presentation.summary: One atomic batch for a deliberately easy jump-and-stick exposure before maximal countermovement-jump assessment, with fixed dose, exposure cap, progression, scheduling, and non-diagnostic readiness modifications.

authority_basis.scientific_support: The reviewed ACSM claim identifies the countermovement vertical jump as an assessment-specific jumping task. It supports the task definition only; it does not establish this batch's contact count, effort, rest, progression cap, or recovery rules.
authority_basis.engineering_prior: The six-contact starting dose, RPE 2-4 range, 90-second rest, 25% relative cap, two-contact absolute cap, and modification mappings are explicit conservative engineering priors. Ratification accepts them provisionally and does not relabel them as scientific findings.

exact_artifacts: One introductory exposure-dose policy for a jumping exposure required by the maximal countermovement-jump assessment.
One exposure definition binding the existing countermovement-jump exercise ontology record to jumping contacts.
One exposure-progression cap and one completion-gated progression policy.
One weekly scheduling policy, approved review, and non-diagnostic session-safety policy.
governs: Derivation of a fixed 2-set by 3-repetition easy jump-and-stick exposure when the exact jumping exposure need is current and introductory exposure is required.
A maximum initial total of 6 jump contacts, with 90 seconds rest and target effort RPE 2-4.
Later progression only after complete, technique-compliant exposure and within both relative and absolute exposure caps.
does_not_establish: Medical clearance, tissue readiness, injury prediction, pain tolerance, or permission to ignore concerning symptoms.
That six contacts, RPE 2-4, 90 seconds rest, or either progression cap is an ACSM recommendation or a scientific optimum.
Readiness for maximal jumping after one exposure; the separate recent-exposure gate remains controlling.
An athlete-specific session, scheduled week, completed exposure, or permission to train.
unresolved_limitations: The exact operational constants have not been calibrated against this athlete's response.
A self-observed controlled landing cannot verify force distribution or all technique errors.
The existing countermovement-jump ontology record represents the movement; the dose instructions deliberately constrain this introductory use to easy non-maximal repetitions.
A later planning step must convert the derived introductory dose into a reviewed scheduled session and record the completed exposure.

evidence.title: ACSM Guidelines, 12th edition: countermovement vertical-jump protocol
evidence.supported_use: The guideline identifies and specifies the countermovement vertical jump as a lower-body power field assessment, providing an exact target task for the exposure prerequisite.
evidence.unsupported_specifics: The source does not validate an introductory training dose or this batch's 2 sets, 3 contacts per set, RPE 2-4, 90-second rest, six-contact initial cap, or later progression limits.

weekly_scheduling_policy_review_content.applicability_rationale: Approve only for the owner-alpha introductory jump-exposure pathway: one session per day, an exact exercise binding, and no automatic same-day repeat. The high-fatigue interval is a forward-compatible guardrail; this introductory exposure is intended to stay low fatigue.
weekly_scheduling_policy_review_content.uncertainty: The daily cap and 24-hour high-fatigue interval are conservative engineering constraints, not values extracted from the cited assessment source. The recent-exposure gate and current readiness remain separate controlling rules.

adjustment.description: Add no more than one easy jump contact per set after full compliant completion and exposure-cap validation.

progression_policy.rationale: Progress only after every planned contact was completed at RPE 4 or below with the reviewed reset-and-stick constraints and no post-session safety interruption; the separate exposure validator must also approve the proposed total.

technique_constraints: Perform each repetition as an easy non-maximal vertical jump, then land on both feet under control.
Pause, regain a stable quiet stance, and deliberately reset before the next repetition; do not rebound continuously.
Stop the exposure for pain, dizziness, instability, an uncontrolled landing, or inability to keep the effort easy.
introductory_exposure_dose_policy.rationale: Use the smallest practical multi-set exposure that lets the athlete rehearse separate easy takeoffs and controlled landings while generating an observable response before any maximal assessment attempt.
introductory_exposure_dose_policy.uncertainty: Every numeric value is a provisional engineering prior. The assessment source defines the target task but does not establish this dose or guarantee that completing it makes maximal jumping appropriate.

exposure_definition.rationale: Count each separately reset countermovement-jump repetition as one jumping exposure contact; intensity and technique remain prescription constraints rather than a different exercise identity.

exposure_progression_policy.rationale: Refuse an unbounded first or subsequent increase: the initial exposure is capped at six contacts, and later proposals must stay within both a 25 percent relative increase and two-contact absolute increase over recent completed exposure.

session_safety_policy.rationale: Permit only conservative reductions for ordinary limited readiness, soreness, sleep disruption, or schedule limitation. Concerning symptoms and failed landing control remain stop conditions governed outside this modification policy.

release.release_rationale: Install the minimum explicit authorities needed to turn a governed missing jumping-exposure prerequisite into a bounded, inspectable introductory dose without inventing an athlete capability score or asking the owner to author technical constants.
release.release_uncertainty: The movement association is evidence-linked, but all exact dose, cap, recovery, progression, and modification values are provisional engineering priors. Ratification creates reusable authorities only; athlete-specific derivation, session review, scheduling, and execution remain separate steps.
